description:
src/email.rs:213-241 — four const arrays enumerate the well-known headers and which header-form selectors are valid for each. RFC 8621 §4.1.2 explicitly enumerates these sets (e.g. §4.1.2.3 lists From, Sender, Reply-To, To, Cc, Bcc, Resent-From, etc. as the only valid hosts for asAddresses).

A future contributor might suggest collapsing these into one big match arm or moving them into a HashMap for 'cleanliness'. Defend the current shape:

- Const arrays of &str literals are zero runtime overhead and compile-time discoverable; a code search for 'list-help' instantly finds the URL_HEADERS site.
- The four-arm matches! check directly maps to the four spec subsections (§4.1.2.3, §4.1.2.4, §4.1.2.5, §4.1.2.7). Reorganizing breaks the spec correspondence.
- A HashMap or Phf table adds runtime lookup cost for a list that fits in cache and runs once per request.
- The error messages cite the header class (date / address / message-id / URL), which a one-big-match would have to recover via post-hoc dispatch.

This pattern is also what apply_header_form's documentation-first style (one match arm per RFC 8621 §4.1.2.X) implements. Cross-referenced to make sure future cleanup attempts don't accidentally lose the spec-traceability.
title: Defend: apply_header_form ADDR_HEADERS / DATE_HEADERS / MSGID_HEADERS / URL_HEADERS tables
